senses.def: cows and bulls kept on a farm for milk or meat
examples: The farmer raises cattle on two thousand acres in Texas.
Hundreds of cattle died during the drought.

note: Always plural: "The cattle are grazing". You can't say "a cattle"; say "a cow" or "ten head of cattle".

senses.def: the person or thing that makes something happen
examples: Investigators are still trying to find the cause of the fire.
Heart disease is the leading cause of death in the US.

senses.tr: dava, amaç, uğruna mücadele edilen şey
senses.def: an aim or idea that people support or fight for
examples: The concert raised money for a good cause.

senses.def: to make something happen, especially something bad
examples: The storm caused serious damage to the coast.
I'm sorry for causing you so much trouble.

note: "Cause for" means reason for a feeling: There is no cause for alarm. Pattern: cause someone to do something.

senses.def: great care taken to avoid danger or mistakes
examples: Drivers should use caution on icy roads.
Investors are treating the new market with caution.

senses.def: to warn someone about a possible danger or problem
examples: Doctors caution against taking these pills with alcohol.

collocations: err on the side of caution
note: "Err on the side of caution" means choose the safer option. A "cautionary tale" is a story that warns.

senses.def: careful to avoid risks or mistakes
examples: Banks have become more cautious about lending money.
She's cautious about sharing personal information online.

note: "Cautiously optimistic" is common in news: hopeful but careful.

senses.def: a large natural hole in the side of a hill or under the ground
examples: The hikers took shelter from the storm in a cave.
Ancient paintings were found on the cave walls.

senses.def: to finally agree to something after resisting (cave in)
examples: The company caved in to the workers' demands.

note: "Cave in" also means a roof or wall falling down inward.

senses.def: a small disc on which music or data is recorded
examples: My dad still listens to his old CDs in the car.
The software used to come on a CD.

note: Short for "compact disc". Mostly replaced by streaming today.

senses.def: to stop happening or existing, or to stop doing something
examples: The factory ceased production in 2019.
Her kindness never ceases to amaze me.

note: Formal. In everyday speech, say "stop". A "ceasefire" is an agreement to stop fighting (ateşkes).

senses.def: the inside surface at the top of a room
examples: The apartment has high ceilings and big windows.
There's a crack in the bathroom ceiling.

senses.def: an upper limit on prices, wages, or amounts
examples: Congress voted to raise the debt ceiling.

note: The "glass ceiling" is an invisible barrier stopping women or minorities from reaching top jobs.

senses.def: to do something enjoyable because of a special day or event
examples: We went out to dinner to celebrate our anniversary.
Fans celebrated in the streets after the final.

senses.def: to praise someone or something publicly
examples: The festival celebrates the city's immigrant communities.

note: You celebrate an event, not a person: "celebrate her birthday". To speak to the person, say "congratulate".

senses.def: a party or special event organized to celebrate something
examples: The New Year's celebrations went on until morning.
Her promotion calls for a celebration!

senses.def: a famous person, especially in entertainment
examples: The restaurant is popular with Hollywood celebrities.
She became an overnight celebrity after her video went viral.

senses.def: the state of being famous
examples: He struggled to deal with his sudden celebrity.

note: "Celeb" is an informal short form.

senses.def: the smallest unit of a living thing
examples: The human body contains trillions of cells.
Cancer cells grow and divide very quickly.

senses.def: a small room where a prisoner is kept
examples: He spent the night in a police cell.

senses.def: (American, informal) a cell phone
examples: Call me on my cell if you're running late.

note: Americans say "cell phone" or "cell"; British speakers say "mobile".

senses.def: an area of land where dead people are buried
examples: Her grandparents are buried in the cemetery outside town.
We walked through an old military cemetery.

note: A "graveyard" is often next to a church; a "cemetery" usually is not. Spelling: -tery, not -tary.

senses.def: a coin or unit of money worth one hundredth of a dollar or euro
examples: The candy costs ninety-nine cents.
Gas prices went up ten cents a gallon this week.

note: Americans call a one-cent coin a "penny". "My two cents" means my opinion. Percent is one word in American English.

senses.def: the middle point or part of something
examples: Place the vase in the center of the table.
Our hotel is right in the center of the city.

senses.def: a building or place used for a particular activity
examples: The new community center offers free classes.

senses.def: to have something as the main subject or focus (center on/around)
examples: The debate centered on the rising cost of housing.

note: American spelling: center. British spelling: centre. Use "center on", not "center about".

senses.def: in or near the middle of a place or object
examples: They live in a central part of the city, close to everything.
Snow is expected across central Europe.

senses.def: most important or main
examples: Education is central to the president's plan.

senses.def: controlled from one main place
examples: The central bank raised interest rates again.

senses.def: a period of one hundred years
examples: The church was built in the twelfth century.
Life has changed enormously over the last century.

note: The 1900s are "the twentieth century". "Turn of the century" means the years around 1900 or 2000.

senses.def: a formal public or religious event with traditional actions
examples: The wedding ceremony took place in a small chapel.
The awards ceremony will be broadcast live.

senses.def: formal behavior on special occasions
examples: The new president was sworn in without much ceremony.

note: "Without ceremony" means quickly, with no fuss.

senses.def: completely sure about something
examples: I'm certain I locked the door before we left.
Are you certain this is the right address?

senses.def: sure to happen or be true
examples: Without a cure, the disease leads to certain death.
It's almost certain that prices will rise.

senses.def: used to refer to particular people or things without naming them
examples: Certain foods can trigger migraines.

note: "To a certain extent" means partly. "A certain" before a name means you don't know them: a certain Mr. Jones.

senses.def: without any doubt
examples: The new design is certainly an improvement.
He certainly knows how to tell a good story.

senses.def: used to agree or give permission politely
examples: "Could you help me with this?" "Certainly."

senses.def: the state of being completely sure
examples: Nobody can say with any certainty what will happen next year.
Scientists know with near certainty that the climate is warming.

senses.def: something that is sure to happen
examples: Victory was a certainty after the first half.

senses.def: an official document that proves certain facts are true
examples: You'll need your birth certificate to apply for a passport.
Everyone who finishes the course gets a certificate.

note: A "gift certificate" (American) is a voucher you give as a present.

senses.def: a series of metal rings joined together, used for fastening or pulling
examples: She wore a gold chain around her neck.
Lock your bike to the rack with a chain.

senses.def: a group of stores, hotels, or restaurants owned by one company
examples: The coffee chain plans to open 200 new stores.

senses.def: a series of connected events or things
examples: The accident set off a chain of events that nobody expected.

senses.def: to fasten someone or something with a chain
examples: Protesters chained themselves to the gates.

note: A "chain reaction" is a series of events where each causes the next.

senses.def: a seat for one person, with a back and usually four legs
examples: Pull up a chair and join us.
This office chair hurts my back.

senses.def: the person in charge of a meeting or committee
examples: She was elected chair of the board last year.

senses.def: to be in charge of a meeting or committee
examples: The senator chairs the committee on energy.

note: "Sit on a chair" but "sit in an armchair". "Chair" is a gender-neutral title for chairman.

senses.def: the person who leads a meeting, committee, or company board
examples: The chairman opened the meeting at nine o'clock.
He stepped down as chairman after twenty years.

note: Many organizations now prefer the neutral "chair" or "chairperson". Plural: chairmen.

senses.def: a difficult task that tests someone's ability
examples: Climate change is one of the biggest challenges we face.
Running a marathon was a real challenge for me.

senses.def: to question whether something is right, true, or legal
examples: The company plans to challenge the decision in court.
Good teachers challenge students to think for themselves.

senses.def: to invite someone to compete or fight
examples: He challenged his brother to a game of chess.

note: In English, "challenge" often has a positive feel: a test you can grow from.

senses.def: difficult in a way that tests your ability, often in an interesting way
examples: Teaching teenagers is challenging but rewarding.
The past year has been very challenging for small businesses.

note: Often used as a polite word for "difficult" in work and business contexts.

senses.def: a hall used for formal meetings, or one of the parts of a parliament
examples: The senators returned to the chamber for the final vote.
The bill must pass both chambers of Congress.

senses.def: an enclosed space in a body, machine, or building
examples: The heart has four chambers.

note: A "chamber of commerce" (ticaret odası) is a group of local businesses.

senses.def: a person or team that has won a competition
examples: She is the current world champion in the 100 meters.
The defending champions lost in the first round.

senses.def: someone who publicly fights for a cause or group
examples: He was a lifelong champion of workers' rights.

senses.def: to publicly support or fight for a cause
examples: The senator has championed clean energy for years.

senses.def: a competition to find the best player or team in a sport
examples: The team is competing in the national championship this weekend.
She won her first world championship at nineteen.

senses.def: the position of being a champion
examples: They held the championship for three years in a row.

senses.def: the possibility that something will happen
examples: There's a good chance it will rain tomorrow.
What are the chances of winning the lottery?

senses.def: an opportunity to do something
examples: I never got a chance to thank her.
This is your last chance to apply.

senses.def: the way things happen without being planned
examples: We met by chance at a friend's party.

note: Turkish "şans" often means luck; English "chance" means possibility or opportunity. For luck, say "luck": Good luck!

senses.def: to become different, or to make something different
examples: The town has changed a lot since I was a kid.
She changed her mind at the last minute.

senses.def: to replace one thing with another, such as clothes or trains
examples: I need to change trains in Philadelphia.
Give me a minute to change out of my work clothes.

senses.def: the act or result of something becoming different
examples: The new manager made a lot of changes.

senses.def: coins, or the money you get back when you pay more than the price
examples: Keep the change.
Do you have change for a twenty?

note: "For a change" means doing something different from usual: Let's eat out for a change.

senses.def: a television station or an online video account
examples: What channel is the game on?
She started a cooking channel on YouTube.

senses.def: a way of communicating or sending information or goods
examples: Complaints should go through the proper channels.

senses.def: a passage of water connecting two seas, or a narrow route for water
examples: Ships crossed the English Channel at night.

senses.def: to direct money, energy, or ideas toward a particular purpose
examples: He channeled his anger into his music.

note: American spelling: channeled, channeling (British: channelled). A man-made waterway is a "canal", not a channel.

senses.def: a state of complete confusion and lack of order
examples: The snowstorm caused chaos on the roads.
The kitchen was in total chaos after the party.

note: Pronounced /ˈkeɪɑːs/ (KAY-oss). Uncountable: "a lot of chaos", not "a chaos".

senses.def: one of the main sections of a book, usually with a number or title
examples: Read the first three chapters before next class.
The final chapter reveals who the killer is.

senses.def: a period of time in someone's life or in history
examples: Moving abroad opened a new chapter in her life.

senses.def: (American) a local branch of a club or organization
examples: She runs the Boston chapter of the charity.

note: "Chapter 11" (American) is a type of bankruptcy that lets a company keep operating.

senses.def: a person or animal in a book, play, or movie
examples: The main character is a detective in 1920s Chicago.
Which character did you like most?

senses.def: all the qualities that make up a person's personality, especially moral qualities
examples: Losing with dignity shows real strength of character.

senses.def: the special qualities that make a place or thing different from others
examples: The old houses give the neighborhood its character.

senses.def: a letter, number, or symbol used in writing
examples: Passwords must be at least eight characters long.

note: "Out of character" means unusual for that person: It was out of character for him to shout.

senses.def: a typical quality or feature of someone or something
examples: Patience is one of the key characteristics of a good teacher.
The two species share many physical characteristics.

senses.def: very typical of a particular person, place, or thing
examples: She answered with her characteristic honesty.
The sharp taste is characteristic of this type of cheese.

senses.def: to be a typical feature of something
examples: The region is characterized by hot summers and mild winters.
Long working hours characterize the industry.

senses.def: to describe someone or something as having particular qualities
examples: The minister characterized the protests as peaceful.

note: Very common in the passive: "be characterized by". British spelling: characterise.

senses.def: to ask for money for goods or a service
examples: The hotel charges forty dollars a night for parking.
They didn't charge us for the extra bags.

senses.def: the amount of money asked for something
examples: Delivery is free of charge for orders over fifty dollars.

senses.def: to formally accuse someone of a crime
examples: He was charged with theft and released on bail.

senses.def: to put electricity into a battery
examples: I need to charge my phone before we leave.

note: "In charge of" means responsible for: She's in charge of marketing. "Charge" is also an accusation: face charges.

senses.def: an organization that collects money to help people in need
examples: She volunteers for a charity that helps homeless people.
All the money raised will go to charity.

senses.def: money or help given to people in need
examples: The family refused to accept charity from neighbors.

note: Americans often say "nonprofit" for a charity organization. "Charity begins at home" is a common saying.

senses.def: the quality of being pleasant and attractive
examples: The old town has a lot of charm.
He used all his charm to get a table at the restaurant.

senses.def: a small object believed to bring good luck
examples: She wears a lucky charm around her neck.

senses.def: to please or attract someone
examples: The puppy charmed everyone at the party.

note: "Work like a charm" means work very well. Turkish "nazar boncuğu" can be called an "evil eye charm".

senses.def: very pleasant or attractive
examples: We stayed in a charming little hotel by the sea.
Her husband is a charming man with a great sense of humor.

note: "Prince Charming" means an ideal romantic partner, often used ironically.

senses.def: a drawing, diagram, or table that shows information
examples: The chart shows how sales have grown since 2020.
The nurse checked the patient's chart.

senses.def: a weekly list of the most popular songs or albums (the charts)
examples: Her new single went straight to number one on the charts.

senses.def: to record or follow the progress of something
examples: The documentary charts the rise of social media.

note: "Uncharted territory/waters" means a new, unknown situation.

senses.def: an official document that sets out the rights, aims, or rules of a group
examples: The UN Charter was signed in 1945.
The city's charter gives the mayor wide powers.

senses.def: the act of renting a plane, boat, or bus for a particular trip
examples: We booked a charter flight to the islands.

senses.def: to rent a plane, boat, or bus for private use
examples: The team chartered a plane for the away game.

note: A "charter school" (American) is publicly funded but run independently.

senses.def: to run or drive after someone or something to catch them
examples: The dog chased the cat up a tree.
Police chased the stolen car for twenty miles.

senses.def: to try hard to get something you want
examples: Too many young people chase fame instead of building skills.

senses.def: the act of following someone quickly in order to catch them
examples: The movie ends with an exciting car chase through the city.

note: "Cut to the chase" means get to the main point quickly.

senses.def: to talk in a friendly, informal way
examples: We chatted for hours over coffee.
I chatted with a woman on the train about her trip.

senses.def: a friendly, informal conversation
examples: Let's have a quick chat after the meeting.

senses.def: a written conversation online
examples: Send me the link in the group chat.

note: "Chat" is always friendly and informal; for serious talks, use "discuss" or "talk".

senses.def: costing little money
examples: Fruit is cheap at the farmers' market in summer.
We found a cheap flight to Lisbon.

senses.def: low in quality; or (American) unwilling to spend money
examples: The cheap shoes fell apart after a month.
Don't be so cheap; leave a proper tip.

senses.def: (informal) for a low price
examples: I got this sofa really cheap at a garage sale.

note: "Cheap" can suggest poor quality; "inexpensive" or "affordable" sound more positive.

senses.def: to act dishonestly to win or gain an advantage
examples: He was caught cheating on his final exam.
Players who cheat will be banned.

senses.def: to have a secret sexual relationship outside your marriage or relationship (cheat on)
examples: She found out her boyfriend had been cheating on her.

senses.def: a person who cheats
examples: Everyone knew he was a cheat at cards.

note: Americans more often say "cheater" for the person. "Cheat on a test" (American) / "cheat in an exam" (British).

senses.def: to look at something to make sure it is correct, safe, or as expected
examples: Always check your answers before handing in the test.
Can you check whether the store is open?

senses.def: an examination to make sure something is correct or safe
examples: Airport staff carried out security checks on every bag.

senses.def: (American) the bill in a restaurant; also a written order to a bank to pay money
examples: Could we have the check, please?
My grandmother still pays her rent by check.

note: British spelling for the bank document is "cheque". "Keep something in check" means control it.

senses.def: either side of the face below the eyes
examples: She kissed her grandmother on the cheek.
Tears ran down his cheeks.

note: "Tongue in cheek" means not serious, joking. In British English, "cheek" also means rude, disrespectful talk.
